betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Satellites need power to stay alive in orbit, and that means solar panels.

The §6Small Solar Panel§f generates 10 RF/t in direct sunlight, while the §6Large Solar Panel§f bumps that to 40 RF/t. You'll also want a §6Satellite Battery§f to buffer power during eclipses when the panel goes dark.

These get launched as part of the satellite assembly, so plan your payload before launch. A satellite without power dies within a day. For long-duration missions, the large panel is basically mandatory, the small one just can't keep up.

The panels only work in direct sunlight, so a polar orbit keeps them out of planetary shadow longer. And yes, they do stop working if the satellite passes behind a planet or station.

§ePS:§f The battery tiers scale with capacity. Higher tiers let your satellite survive longer eclipses.
